issues.description: selector-not-notation regex `/:not\(/i` changes case sensitivity vs. prior `includes(':not(')`
issues.detail: The original guard used a case-sensitive substring check; the new walkRules filter is case-insensitive. CSS pseudo-classes are case-insensitive per spec so this is arguably more correct, but it is a subtle behavior change that should be called out in the changeset or covered by a test. Rules with `:NOT(` will now be evaluated where previously they were skipped.

issues.description: font-weight HAS_NUMERIC may false-skip when `font` shorthand contains numeric weight adjacent to non-word chars handled by tokenizer
issues.detail: HAS_NUMERIC is `\b(?:100|...|900)\b` tested against the raw declaration value. The `font` shorthand can also legitimately contain values that the parser later treats as weight via tokenization. While `\b` is generally safe, the fast-path bypasses parsing entirely; any edge case where a weight is encoded with surrounding punctuation valueParser would still recognize but the regex would not is now silently skipped. Worth a unit test covering shorthand edge cases.

issues.description: import-notation fast-path may miss invalid mixed content in `url` mode
issues.detail: `if (primary === 'url' && /url\(/i.test(params)) return;` skips any params containing `url(`. If a malformed `@import` contains both a bare string and a `url()` (e.g. authoring mistake), the original code would have parsed it and potentially reported; the new code short-circuits. Confirm there is no diagnostic path inside checkAtRuleImportParams that fires for url-mode params containing url().

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation `context` regex `/(?:min|max)-/i` can false-positive on values like `min-content`
issues.detail: The regex matches any occurrence of `min-` or `max-`, including value tokens such as `min-content`/`max-content` inside `@media (width: min-content)`. This only causes unnecessary parsing (no correctness impact) but undermines the perf benefit for queries that legitimately contain those tokens without prefix features. Anchoring to feature-name position would be tighter.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE assumes PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS values are regex-safe
issues.detail: `HAS_PERCENTAGE` builds a RegExp by joining PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS values directly without escaping. Today those values are likely `0%`/`100%` which contain no regex metacharacters, but the pattern is fragile to future additions (e.g. parenthesized forms). Wrap with an escape helper for safety.

issues.description: Changeset entry is too terse to communicate scope
issues.detail: `Fixed: *-notation performance` does not indicate which rules were touched or what users should expect. Since six rules are affected, a slightly expanded changeset (listing the affected rule names) would help downstream consumers triaging perf regressions.

review.summary: This PR adds fast-path regex guards to six `*-notation` rules so they skip parsing when no violation is possible. The optimizations are generally well-targeted and skip in the safe direction (parsing extra is fine; skipping wrongly would be a regression). Main concerns: the selector-not-notation guard changes case sensitivity vs. the prior substring check, the import-notation `url` mode skip is aggressive (any `url(` substring causes a skip), and the regexes built from token lists assume the tokens contain no regex metacharacters. No P0 issues; recommend tightening tests for shorthand and mixed cases before merge.
